newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra mulls support for sheep disease fight.
newsitem.headline: Canberra mulls support for sheep disease fight.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it wanted to assess the spread of the fatal Ovine Johne's sheep disease before funding efforts to combat it.

Primary Industries Minister John Anderson, responding to concerns that inaction over the disease was crippling farm business, said a full asessment was needed before deciding on a strategy and providing money.
"I will certainly look closely again at what we can do," Anderson told a rural conference.
"I am aware of the seriousness of the problem."
The disease is well established in New South Wales, but it was not known how much of the state is affected.
The New South Wales Farmers Association has urged a programme to monitor, control and eradicate the disease, in which sheep waste away after eating infected pasture.
The association said it would begin an eradication programme in September if it was feasible and cost effective.
The NSW government had provided A$300,000, but the association said more money was needed.
